sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 46.6% a year, from $6.91 billion in FY2017 to $216 billion in FY2026 [F211][F1][F10].
Revenue was flat in FY2023, up 0.2% [D284], then rose 125.9% to $60.9 billion in FY2024 [D338][F8].
FY2025 added 114.2% to $130 billion [D393][F9], which the filing ties to data center compute and networking platforms for AI [P16].
Data Center products were 88.3% of FY2025 revenue [D617] and supplied 111.1pp of that year's growth [D619].
In FY2026 the filing credits Blackwell and NVLink demand, with Data Center computing up 58.9% and networking up 141.5% [P8][D628][D635].
Data Center supplied 60.2pp of FY2026's 65.5% revenue growth [D622][D448], and Compute & Networking is 89.6% of revenue [D739].
Operating expenses rose 40.7% against 65.5% revenue growth, an incremental operating margin of 57.3% [D468][D448][D475].
In FY2026 diluted EPS grew 66.7% against 64.7% net income growth, while the diluted share count fell 1.2% [D452][D450][D470].
Operating margin was 60.4% in FY2026 [F50], against a window median of 32.8% [D813] and a window high of 62.4% [D812].
Gross margin fell 3.9pp to 71.1% [D462][F30], more than explaining the 2.0pp operating margin decline [D477][D463].
The filings cited do not explain the FY2026 gross margin fall; they tie a $4.5 billion H20 charge to Compute & Networking profit [P7][D462].
Operating expenses rose 41% on employee growth and compute infrastructure costs [P9][D468].
Other income of $11.1 billion [X120], mainly unrealized equity gains [P3], was taxed at 15.1% [D434], leaving net margin at 55.6% [F70] against 60.4% operating [F50].
Free cash flow was $96.7 billion [F110], 0.81x net income [D436], just below the 0.83x window median [D828].
Operating cash flow was 0.86x net income [D435]; inventory grew 112.3% [D474] against 65.5% revenue growth [D448], and the filings cited do not explain the build.
Capex was $6.04 billion [F105], 2.8% of revenue [D431] and 2.13x D&A [D437].
Net cash fell to $2.14 billion [D441] from $34.7 billion [D386], or 1.0% of revenue [D442].
That ranks at the 83rd percentile of six semis peers, above a peer median of -13.9% [D844][D845].
FY2026 short-term investments are missing from the pack, so cash and investments equals cash alone [D439][F150], and the net cash drop may be overstated [D441].
Buybacks of $40.1 billion [X150] and dividends of $974 million [X160] took 42.5% of free cash flow [D444].
Inventory provisions cut FY2023 gross margin by 8.0pp [D298], with $2.17 billion of charges on excess Ampere supply [P35][P38].
The pattern recurred in FY2026, when an H20 excess-inventory charge hit Compute & Networking profit [P7].
Two direct customers at 22% and 14% of FY2026 revenue [P6] make concentration the main risk to the 89.6% segment share [D739].
The FY2023 Graphics drop of 25.0% [D754] is not a live flag, since Graphics grew 57.0% in FY2026 [D747].
Gross margin falling below its 62.2% window median [D819], from 71.1% [F30], would show the mix gain reversing in the FY2027 10-K.
Inventory growth dropping below the 65.5% revenue growth [D448], from 112.3% [D474], would show the build clearing in the FY2027 10-K.
Reported cash and investments returning near FY2025's $43.2 billion [D384] would confirm the FY2026 net cash of $2.14 billion [D441] omitted investments [D439].
